Entry Hunting Rights and Woodlands Forests provided wood, game, charcoal, and hiding places, but were often enclosed by the lord's hunting rights. Nobles regard deer hunting as training and recreation, while villagers may be punished for a poached rabbit; the same forest may be glory, food, or legal trap in the eyes of different people. Whether it is valid depends on who can grant the rights, collect the consideration, and actually make the judgment come to fruition in the event of default.

If a rule is practiced over and over again, it will find its way into rituals, crafts, and prayers; if it is sustained only by fear, cracks will show at the onset of a crisis.
